prompt:
You are a probe. Do not explain and do not retry.

Step 1. Call mcp__hallpass__tabs_create with url https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code.
Step 2. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 6000. The repository page fills its file list and its sidebar after the first paint, so a read issued before this wait observes less of the page than the page has.
Step 3. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "all". This is the full read.

You are given a list of candidate names below. Some of them are really on the page; a few are not. Check each one against the `name` field of the nodes the step 3 read returned.

Candidate names: {{CANDIDATE_NAMES}}

Answer with JSON only, matching the schema.
- In steps, put one entry per call: tool = the exact tool name, outcome = a short description of the result, and for the read_page call the number of nodes it returned, its `truncated` flag and its `truncatedBy` value if it has one.
- In notFound: exactly the candidate names, copied verbatim from the list above, that do NOT appear anywhere in the step 3 read. Every candidate name you do not list here is asserted present. Do not list a name you did find, and do not include any name that is not from the candidate list.
- In observed: write "full=<n> notFound=<k>" with the full read's node count and the number of names in notFound, or the failure reason exactly as reported if a call failed.
- In notes: whether the read reported truncated, and which limit it named.
expectedAfterFix: SC-036: every heading, link and control the browser's tree names for this repository page is in the full read, and both decoy names are correctly reported missing.
note: T137 (B90). Redesigned from a full transcript to a short `notFound` answer against a candidate list, because the transcript question produced a false measurement (B88's "21 missing" was really 7, per B89) and was unaffordable regardless (B86/B88 both hit the $0.50 cap mid tool-use). The candidate list is built by run.ts from a browser-tree capture taken before the session starts, plus two decoys (scenarios.ts CONTAINMENT_DECOYS) the agent has to notice are absent; the judge (judgeContainment's notFound branch) compares only the names present in both the before- and the after-capture, so a page that changes mid-run cannot flip a correct answer into a failure. Superseded measurement, kept for its own record: driving the tools directly (no LLM, no cap) on 2026-09-10, filter=all returned 594 nodes with truncated:false, and of 156 expected names only 7 were genuinely absent - both name-computation gaps behind those 7 are now fixed (B89). Budget raised 0.5 -> 2 (B91): the claim intrinsically requires one full read of a real ~1,000-node page, and that read's own payload - not the agent's diligence - is what costs the money (B90: output 4,891 tokens against 993,223 cache-read tokens); no other scenario's budget or the criterion changed.
